t: The chapter of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 that deals with insurance of motor vehicles against third party risks is:
e: Chapter XI (Sections 145 to 164D) of the 1988 Act covers compulsory insurance; the corresponding provisions in the 1939 Act were in Chapter VIII. Chapter XII deals with Claims Tribunals.

t: In the Indian motor insurance context, 'detariffing' of 2007 resulted in which of the following?
o: Insurers were free to price OD risks but had to continue using standard policy wordings
Insurers could change policy wordings but not prices
e: From 1 January 2007 insurers could fix OD premium rates subject to IRDAI's file-and-use norms, but policy wordings, terms and conditions of the erstwhile tariff remained standardised. TP rates stayed regulated.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 148 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a policy condition restricting cover by reference to the age or condition of the vehicle, the driver's age or the horse-power of the vehicle is:
o: Of no effect as regards the insurer's liability to third parties under the Act
e: Section 148 ('avoidance of restrictions on scope of policy') makes such restrictive conditions ineffective in respect of third party liabilities covered under Section 147, although they may be enforced between insurer and insured.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), driving a vehicle without a valid driving licence is punishable with a fine of up to:
e: The 2019 amendment raised the penalty for driving without a licence to imprisonment up to three months or fine up to ₹5,000 or both; drunken driving under Section 185 attracts ₹10,000.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under the Central Motor Vehicles (Fifth Amendment) Rules, 2022 (Rule 150A), the police must submit the First Accident Report (FAR) to the Claims Tribunal within:
e: The 2022 rules fix a schedule: FAR within 48 hours, Interim Accident Report within 50 days and Detailed Accident Report within 90 days, with the insurer's designated officer to settle within 30 days of the DAR.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Which of the following sections of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was DELETED by the 2019 amendment?
o: Section 163A (special provisions for structured formula compensation)
e: Sections 140 to 144 (interim no-fault liability) and 163A/163B (structured formula) were omitted and replaced by the new Section 164 scheme of ₹5 lakh / ₹2.5 lakh.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 161 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'hit and run motor accident' means an accident arising out of the use of a motor vehicle:
o: Where the driver flees even if the vehicle number is known
The identity whereof cannot be ascertained in spite of reasonable efforts
e: The defining feature is that the vehicle cannot be identified; if the vehicle is identified, the ordinary Tribunal remedy against its owner and insurer applies rather than the hit-and-run scheme.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 165 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Claims Tribunal adjudicates claims for:
o: Death, bodily injury and damage to property of third parties arising from use of motor vehicles
Own damage disputes between insurer and insured
e: Tribunals handle compensation for death or bodily injury and for damage to any property of a third party arising out of motor accidents. OD disputes go to arbitration, consumer fora or civil courts.

t: As per the IDV depreciation schedule, a vehicle aged more than 2 years but not more than 3 years attracts depreciation of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The schedule is: up to 6 months 5%; 6 months to 1 year 15%; 1 to 2 years 20%; 2 to 3 years 30%; 3 to 4 years 40%; 4 to 5 years 50%. Beyond 5 years IDV is fixed by mutual agreement.

topic: Motor Vehicles Act and Legal Framework
t: Under Section 151 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, if the insured becomes insolvent after incurring a third party liability:
o: The third party loses the right to compensation
The insurer is discharged from liability
The claim must be filed with the Official Liquidator only
The insured's rights against the insurer are transferred to and vest in the third party
e: Section 151 protects victims by vesting the insured's rights under the policy in the third party on the insured's insolvency or winding up, so the insurer still pays the victim.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: From 1 September 2019, IRDAI permitted insurers to issue which type of policy for cars and two-wheelers?
o: Stand-alone own damage policies, since vehicles already carry long-term TP cover
Policies without any TP cover for vehicles kept in garages
Policies without compulsory PA cover for owner-driver in all cases
e: Because new vehicles carry 3- or 5-year TP cover, IRDAI allowed stand-alone annual OD policies from September 2019, provided the vehicle has valid TP cover from the same or another insurer.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'public service vehicle' includes all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Section 2(35) defines public service vehicle as a vehicle used for carriage of passengers for hire or reward, including maxi cab, motor cab, contract carriage and stage carriage. A goods carriage is a separate category.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: A 'bundled' motor policy for a new two-wheeler sold in 2025 typically means:
o: 5-year TP cover together with 1-year OD cover
e: Bundled covers combine the mandatory long-term TP (5 years for two-wheelers, 3 years for cars) with a one-year OD section, after IRDAI withdrew compulsory long-term package policies in 2020.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Which statement about the two-wheeler package policy's 'limitations as to use' is correct?
o: The vehicle may be used for hire or reward
The vehicle may be used for carrying goods for hire
The vehicle may be used for racing with the insurer's oral consent
The vehicle may be used for social, domestic, pleasure and professional purposes but not for hire or reward, racing, pace-making or speed testing
e: Two-wheeler policies mirror private car limitations; commercial use of a two-wheeler (e.g. delivery for hire) requires a commercial vehicle policy, failing which OD claims may be treated as non-standard.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: A tractor used for agricultural purposes is insured under which category?
e: Agricultural tractors, along with cranes, forklifts, road rollers and similar, are rated as miscellaneous and special type vehicles under the commercial vehicle section.

t: The NCB earned after the first claim-free year is:
e: The NCB scale is 20% after one claim-free year, 25% after two, 35% after three, 45% after four and 50% after five or more consecutive claim-free years.

t: A car's OD premium is ₹30,000. It has an ARAI-approved anti-theft device. The anti-theft discount is:
e: 2.5% of ₹30,000 is ₹750, but the discount is capped at ₹500 per vehicle, so ₹500 is allowed.

t: The endorsement for legal liability to a paid driver employed in connection with the insured vehicle (under WC Act) is charged at:
e: Legal liability to paid driver, cleaner or conductor is covered at a flat ₹25 per person per annum; ₹60 is the TP charge for CNG/LPG kits and 4% applies to accessories.

t: Under the depreciation schedule for partial losses, metal parts of a vehicle aged between 1 and 2 years attract depreciation of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The age-based schedule for 'all other parts' is: up to 6 months nil; 6 months–1 year 5%; 1–2 years 10%; 2–3 years 15%; 3–4 years 25%; 4–5 years 35%; 5–10 years 40%; above 10 years 50%.

t: For a 7-year-old private car, how is the IDV determined?
o: By applying 50% depreciation to the listed price
By mutual agreement between the insurer and the insured based on market value
IDV cannot be fixed; only TP cover is available
e: The depreciation schedule ends at 5 years (50%); for older vehicles or obsolete models, IDV is arrived at by mutual agreement considering the market value and surveyor assessment.

t: Under a hire-purchase endorsement, in the event of a total loss claim the insurer:
o: Withholds payment until the loan is repaid
Pays the financier (owner under the agreement) to the extent of its interest, or as jointly agreed
e: The hire-purchase/hypothecation endorsement records the financier's interest; total loss payments are made to or with the consent of the financier, protecting the loan outstanding.

t: The endorsement extending cover for lamps, tyres, tubes, mudguards, bonnet, bumpers, headlights and paintwork of a commercial vehicle for damage in the absence of other damage carries an additional OD premium of:
e: IMT-23 widens the OD cover for commercial vehicles to such parts even when the vehicle is not otherwise damaged, at 15% extra OD premium; the standard policy excludes them unless the vehicle is damaged at the same time.

t: Under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, the form prescribed for a cover note is:
e: Rule 142 prescribes Form 52 for the cover note, valid for 60 days; Form 51 is the certificate of insurance under Rule 141.

t: The 'Drivers' clause of the Indian motor policy covers a person who:
o: Holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident, or had held one and is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence
Has a driving licence from any country
Is named in the proposal form only
e: The clause covers any person including the insured provided he holds an effective driving licence, or had held one and is not disqualified; a learner's licence holder is covered subject to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules.

topic: Types of Motor Vehicles and Policies
t: Under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a 'maxi cab' is a motor vehicle constructed or adapted to carry, excluding the driver:
o: More than 6 but not more than 12 passengers
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 2(22) defines a maxi cab as carrying more than six but not more than twelve passengers excluding the driver, for hire or reward; a motor cab carries up to six.

t: Under Section II (liability) of the private car package policy, liability for death or injury to occupants of the insured car:
o: Is covered only for family members
Is covered only up to ₹1 lakh
Is covered provided they are not carried for hire or reward
e: The package policy liability section extends to persons carried in the private car, except those carried for hire or reward or as employees in the course of employment; the Act itself does not mandate cover for gratuitous occupants.

t: The 'Geographical Area' of a standard Indian motor policy is:
o: India only, unless extended by endorsement IMT-1
e: Cover applies within India; extension to Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Maldives is available by IMT-1 at additional premium.

t: An insured cancels his annual package policy after 7 months at his own request. The OD premium of ₹24,000 is refunded to the extent of:
e: On cancellation at the insured's request the insurer retains premium on short period scale, which is 80% for a period of 7 months. Refund = 20% of ₹24,000 = ₹4,800; had the insurer cancelled, pro-rata refund of 5/12 would apply.

t: Which of the following documents is NOT normally required for a private car own damage (accident) claim?
o: Copy of registration certificate and driving licence
e: Permit and fitness certificate apply to transport vehicles only; a private car claim needs the claim form, RC, DL, estimate/bills and, for theft or third party injury, the FIR.

t: A 'spot survey' is generally conducted when:
o: The accident is major, the vehicle is still at the site, or there is a need to verify the circumstances (e.g. suspected fraud, overloading)
The repair is done at a network garage
e: Spot surveys record the position of the vehicle, load, driver and physical evidence immediately after the accident, before the vehicle is moved, aiding both OD assessment and TP defence.

t: Depreciation applicable to fibre glass components in a partial loss claim is:
e: Fibre glass components attract 30% depreciation, rubber/plastic/battery/tyre items 50%, glass nil and other parts age-based rates.

t: In a cashless claim at a network garage, the insured normally pays which of the following directly to the garage?
o: The full bill, to be reimbursed later
The depreciation, compulsory/voluntary deductible and any non-admissible items
e: Under cashless settlement the insurer pays the admissible amount to the garage; the insured bears depreciation (unless nil-dep add-on), deductibles and items outside cover such as consumables.

t: A 9-year-old car (IDV ₹2,50,000) suffers accident damage: metal parts ₹1,00,000, labour ₹20,000, paint material (separately billed) ₹10,000, paint labour ₹8,000. Compulsory deductible ₹1,000. Claim payable is:
e: Metal parts at 40% depreciation (5–10 years): ₹60,000; labour ₹20,000; paint material at 50%: ₹5,000; paint labour ₹8,000. Total ₹93,000 less ₹1,000 deductible = ₹92,000.

t: Licensing of insurance surveyors and loss assessors in India is governed by:
o: Section 64UM of the Insurance Act, 1938 and IRDAI regulations
Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
e: Section 64UM read with the IRDAI (Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors) Regulations, 2015 governs licensing, categorisation and duties of surveyors.

t: A car with IDV ₹5,00,000 has an accident with assessed repair cost of ₹3,90,000 and salvage value of the wreck ₹70,000. Which settlement is correct if the insurer takes the wreck?
o: Total loss: pay IDV of ₹5,00,000 less compulsory deductible, insurer retains salvage
Total loss: pay ₹4,30,000 and insurer retains salvage
e: Repair cost is 78% of IDV, above the 75% CTL threshold. With the insurer taking the wreck, the claim is IDV less the deductible; salvage value is deducted only when the insured retains the wreck.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: In National Insurance Co. v. Baljit Kaur (2004), concerning a gratuitous passenger in a goods vehicle, the Supreme Court directed that:
o: The insurer must pay the award to the claimant and recover it from the owner of the vehicle
The insurer is not liable and need not pay anything
e: Following Asha Rani, the Court held the insurer not liable in law for gratuitous passengers in goods vehicles but, in the interest of justice, directed 'pay and recover' from the owner.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Pranay Sethi (2017), the future prospects addition for a deceased aged 55 years with a permanent job is:
e: For permanent employees aged 50–60 the addition is 15% (30% for 40–50 and 50% below 40); for self-employed or fixed-salary persons the corresponding figures are 10%, 25% and 40%.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Meera, aged 24, unmarried, salaried with a permanent job earning ₹25,000 per month, dies in an accident. Her parents claim compensation. Using Pranay Sethi and Sarla Verma, the loss of dependency is:
e: Annual income ₹3,00,000 + 50% future prospects = ₹4,50,000; deduct 50% for personal expenses (bachelor) = ₹2,25,000; multiplier for age up to 25 is 18; ₹2,25,000 × 18 = ₹40,50,000.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the award of the Claims Tribunal must specify:
o: The amount payable by the insurer, owner or driver, and the persons to whom compensation is to be paid with apportionment among them
e: Section 168 requires the Tribunal to specify the amount payable by the insurer or owner or driver, and in the case of multiple claimants, apportion the compensation among them.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Under the Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme, 2022, the compensation for grievous hurt is:
e: The 2022 Scheme provides ₹50,000 for grievous hurt and ₹2 lakh for death, replacing the Solatium Scheme's ₹12,500 and ₹25,000.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: The Tribunal finds that the insured's goods truck was driven by a driver holding a fake licence, which the owner had verified in good faith. Based on United India v. Lehru (2003), the likely outcome is:
o: The insurer is liable because the owner is not expected to verify the genuineness of a licence beyond reasonable checks; breach is not wilful
e: In Lehru the Court held that an owner who satisfied himself that the driver had a licence and drove competently cannot be said to have committed a wilful breach; the insurer must pay.

topic: Third Party Liability Claims and MACT
t: Where a third party's claim is for damage to property (say, a shop damaged by the insured's truck), which forum has jurisdiction?
o: The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, as Section 165 covers property damage claims
e: Since 1988, Tribunals adjudicate property damage claims too; the insurer's liability is limited to the policy's TPPD limit (₹7.5 lakh for cars/CVs), with the excess falling on the owner.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: The 'Tyre Protect' add-on covers:
o: Repair or replacement cost of tyres and tubes damaged by cuts, bursts or bulges even without other damage to the vehicle
e: The base policy pays tyres only when the vehicle is otherwise damaged (and then at 50%); tyre protect covers accidental tyre damage on its own, excluding wear and tear.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: A 'floater' motor policy permitted by IRDAI in 2022 allows:
o: A single OD policy covering multiple vehicles owned by the same individual, with a floating sum insured
Cover for vehicles of different owners under one policy
e: The floater concept lets one owner cover several vehicles (e.g. a car and a two-wheeler) under one OD policy, part of IRDAI's 2022 move to encourage telematics and usage-based products.

topic: Add-on Covers, Regulations and Recent Developments
t: An 'EMI Protection' add-on in motor insurance pays:
o: The full loan outstanding on theft
The vehicle loan EMIs for a specified number of months while the vehicle is under repair after an accident, subject to a minimum repair period
e: EMI protect covers loan instalments falling due during a prolonged accidental repair period, easing cash flow for financed vehicles; it is distinct from Return to Invoice or theft cover.

t: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (as per the 2021 pecuniary jurisdiction rules), a District Commission entertains complaints where the value of goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed:
e: The 2021 rules fix District Commission jurisdiction up to ₹50 lakh, State Commission ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore and National Commission above ₹2 crore, based on consideration paid (premium), not the claim amount.

t: The 'Sarathi' database of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways contains:
e: Sarathi holds driving licence data while VAHAN holds registration data; insurers use both to verify licence validity and vehicle particulars at underwriting and claims.

t: Following the MoRTH advisory of 2018, a digital copy of the insurance certificate stored in DigiLocker or the mParivahan app:
o: Is not valid proof of insurance
Is valid and must be accepted by enforcement authorities as equivalent to the physical document
Is valid only in metro cities
e: MoRTH directed that documents in electronic form via DigiLocker/mParivahan be accepted as legally valid under the IT Act, reducing the need to carry physical certificates.
